questions.stemHtml: Match the following Select the correct answer from given below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
1-c, 2-a, 3-b, 4-d
  1. IL-4 - B cells
  2. IL-5 - Eosinophils
  3. IL-9 - Mast cells
  4. IL-13 - Dendritic cells 

CD4+ T cells can be divided into three subsets that produce distinct cytokines and cause different types of inflammation.

TH1 cells secrete IFN-γ and promote classical macrophage activation.

TH2 cells produce IL-4, IL-5, and IL-13, which attract and activate eosinophils and induce alternative macrophage activation 

Cytokines produced

IFN-Y

IL-4, IL-5, IL-13

IL-17, IL-22

Cytokines that induce this subset

IFN-γ, IL-12

IL-4

TGF-B, IL-6, IL-1, IL-23

Immunological reactions triggered

Macrophage activation

Stimulation of IgE production, activation of mast cells and eosinophils

Recruitment of neutrophils, monocytes

Host defense against

Intracellular microbes

Helminthic

Extracellular bacteria, fungi

Role in disease

Immune-mediated chronic inflammatory diseases (often autoimmune)

Allergies

Immune-mediated chronic inflammatory diseases (often autoimmune)

IL-4 functions to promote class switching to IgE in B cells and to stimulate the proliferation of TH2 cells.

IL-5 is important in the development and activation of eosinophils, which play a crucial role in type I hypersensitivity reactions.

IL-13 stimulates IgE production and induces mucus secretion in epithelial cells. TH2 cells and other cells, such as mast cells, produce chemokines that attract other TH2 cells and leukocytes to the site of the reaction. IL-13 can also induce differentiation in dendritic cells and shares functional similarities with IL-4


IL-9 Main function is promote mast cell growth and function




Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease - 10th edition - page 202-206, 683-686

questions.solutionHtml:
Acid hematin
  • The instrument given in the image is Sahli’s haemoglobinometer, it measures acid hematin.
  • Sahli’s hemoglobinometer: It is used to determine haemoglobin content in blood samples by converting haemoglobin into hematin acid and then diluted produces hematin acid colour which matches with the comparator

questions.stem: Adenocarcinoma lung shows the following marker: Napsin P40TTF1synaptophysinChoose the correct options:
questions.solutionHtml:
a,b,c
  • Adenocarcinoma of the lung shows Napsin, P40, and TTF1 markers. Hence, the correct option is A.a,b,c
  • Synaptophysin, on the other hand, is not typically associated with adenocarcinoma lung.
  • It is a marker commonly used to assess neuroendocrine differentiation in tumors, such as small cell lung carcinoma or carcinoid tumors.


Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease - 10th edition - page 718-720

questions.stemHtml: A 10 yr old boy with elevated platelet count, Hb- 9 g/dL, MCV - 60 fl, MCH - 20, pg S.ferritin – 185 Microgram/L , Elevated lymphocytes and neutrophils, What is the type of anaemia?
questions.solutionHtml:
Anaemia of chronic disorder

The given lab values in a patient with anaemia, with elevated serum ferritin is suggestive of anaemia of chronic disease. The peripheral smear shows microcytic anaemia which is typically seen in ACD.




Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of disease - 10th edition - page 644-649

questions.stemHtml: Match the following histological finding with the tumour: Select the correct answer from given below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
a-4, b-1, c-2, d-3
  • Sezary cells - Cells with cerebriform nuclei are seen in cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (mycosis fungoides type). These cells are characterised by an infolding of nuclear membrane giving them a cerebriform appearance.
  • Faggot cells are highly suggestive of AML M3 (Acute promyelocytic leukemia). Bone marrow histopathology reveals multiple Auer rods in the cytoplasm of promyelocytes.
  • Popcorn cells is a type of Reed Steenberg (RS) cells that are characteristic of lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma
  • Starry sky pattern is the characteristic appearance of Burkitt lymphoma. It is composed of homogenous B-cells with reactive macrophages scattered through the tumour.


Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease - 10th edition - page 601-618

questions.topic: eGurukul · Pathology - INI CET NOV 2022 (PART B)
questions.stem: Regarding papillary carcinoma thyroid Histology. Nuclear clearingNuclear grooving Concentric calcium depositionRecurrent follicleChoose the correct answer?
questions.solutionHtml:
a,b,c,d

The histological features commonly seen in papillary carcinoma of the thyroid  include: 

  1. Nuclear clearing: Papillary carcinoma thyroid often exhibits nuclear clearing or optically clear nuclei, where the nuclei appear empty or pale due to clearing of chromatin.
  2. Nuclear grooving: Papillary carcinoma thyroid is characterized by nuclei with irregular grooves and folds, giving them a "raisinoid" or "coffee bean" appearance.
  3. Concentric calcium deposition: Psammoma bodies, which are concentrically laminated calcific deposits, are frequently seen in papillary carcinoma thyroid. They appear as small, round, and eosinophilic structures.
  4. Recurrent follicle: Papillary carcinoma thyroid may contain recurrent or secondary follicles within the primary thyroid follicles, giving a characteristic feature of papillary structures with surrounding follicles. 

Therefore, the correct answer is B. a, b, c, d.



Robbins Basic Pathology - 9th edition - page 1086-1092

questions.topic: eGurukul · Pathology - INI CET NOV 2022 (PART B)
questions.stem: Choose the correct answer from the following statements Most stomach cancer are hereditaryE-cadherin adhesion defect is seen in diffuse type of gastric caWnt signalling pathway defect is seen in intestinal-type of gastric caDepth of invasion has no prognostic valueChoose the correct answer?
questions.solutionHtml:
b,c
  • Among the given statements, only b and c are correct. Hence, the correct option is C.b,c
  • Most stomach cancer are hereditary: This statement is incorrect. While a small percentage of stomach cancers may have a hereditary component, the majority of stomach cancers are sporadic and not associated with inherited genetic mutations.
  • E-cadherin adhesion defect is seen in diffuse type of gastric ca: This statement is correct. E-cadherin is a cell adhesion molecule, and its loss or dysfunction is a characteristic feature of diffuse-type gastric carcinoma, also known as signet ring cell carcinoma. The loss of E-cadherin contributes to the invasive and diffusely infiltrative growth pattern seen in this type of gastric cancer.
  • Wnt signaling pathway defect is seen in intestinal-type of gastric ca: This statement is correct. The Wnt signaling pathway plays a crucial role in the development of the intestinal-type of gastric cancer.
  • Depth of invasion has no prognostic value: This statement is incorrect. The depth of invasion, also known as tumor stage, is an important prognostic factor in gastric cancer and other malignancies. It provides valuable information about the extent of tumor spread and helps guide treatment decisions and predict patient outcomes.


Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of disease - 9th edition - page 771-773

questions.stem: Identify the correct statements: IL-12 increases production of interferon gammaIL-12 suppresses T cells, inhibits cytotoxicIL-12 inhibits B cellsIL-12 secreted by macrophagesSelect the correct answer form given below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
1 and 4
  • IL-12 is produced by macrophages and increases the production of interferon gamma.
  • IL-12 is produced by dendritic cells and macrophages. Its primary actions are to promote the production of interferon gamma, which increases TH1-type responses and stimulates macrophages. It also promotes differentiation of CD4+ T-cells to Th1 cells.

questions.stemHtml: A 7 year old child with fever, erythematous rash, bone pain, x-ray skull shows multiple lytic lesions, skin biopsy shows prominent nuclear grooves with eosinophils as in the image below. Image shows immunohistochemistry of S100, CD1a. What would be the most likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Langerhans cell histiocytosis
  • The given clinical scenario with the given histological and immunohistochemistry findings is suggestive of Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
  • The histology shows folded nuclei and immunohistochemistry shows positive S100 and CD1a.
  • Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH) is an idiopathic condition characterised by proliferation of abnormal Langerhans (antigen-presenting) cells. The disease has characteristics of both an abnormal reactive process and a neoplastic process. It may present initially as a rash. It can be disseminated and involve the bone marrow, lungs, liver, spleen, lymph nodes, gastrointestinal tract, and pituitary gland. Prognosis varies depending on presentation and organ involvement. LCH can occur at any age but is most common from birth to age 15 years
  • Langerhans cells are dendritic antigen-presenting cells. The abnormal cells in LCH have abnormal proliferation and lower antigen-presenting capability. LCH lesions also contain inflammatory cells and cytokines such as T lymphocytes, eosinophils, neutrophils, and macrophages.


Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Diseases - 10th edition - page 627, 628

questions.stemHtml: The given peripheral smear associated with which type of leukaemia?
questions.solutionHtml:
CLL

The given peripheral smear shows chronic lymphocytic leukaemia. 

Findings of peripheral smear:

  • Predominantly shows small lymphocytes with scanty cytoplasm
  • Smudge cells or basket cells - artefacts of lymphocytes disrupted during making smears.
  • Spherocytes and nucleated RBCs


Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Diseases - 10th edition - page 414, 415, 594-597, 618-623

questions.stem: Which of the following is correct about hereditary spherocytosis?

options.label: C
options.text: Gallstones develop by 4-5 year of age

options.label: D
options.text: At least 25% cases have positive family history

questions.answerText: At least 25% cases have positive family history
questions.solutionHtml:
At least 25% cases have positive family history
  • Hereditary spherocytosis shows 75% autosomal dominant inheritance and 25% have a familial inheritance.
  • Hereditary spherocytosis is a hereditary hemolytic anaemia mostly inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern. It is characterised by mutation of spectrin and ankyrin, RBC surface proteins, which cause disruption of membranes and hemolysis.
  • The disease presents at a young age with severe jaundice and fatigue. Unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia causes gallstones in early adulthood.
  • Peripheral smear shows spherical RBCs without central pallor.
  • MCHC is increased in spherocytosis, whereas MCH is slightly lower due to the anaemia.
  • Splenectomy is the specific treatment. It prevents hemolysis, anaemia and other complications such as gallstones.


Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Diseases - 10th edition - page 638-640

questions.stem: A chronic smoker with 24 pack years presented with breathlessness and chest pain. A lung mass is seen radiologically. On staining, cells are positive for chromogranin. What is the most probable diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Small cell carcinoma lung
  • The given clinical history of smoking and positive staining for chromogranin suggests the diagnosis of Small cell carcinoma lung.
  • It is a type of lung cancer that is strongly associated with smoking. It typically presents with symptoms such as breathlessness and chest pain.
  • Choice of serum tumour markers in patients with small cell lung cancer: chromogranin neuron-specific enolase, and carcinoembryonic antigen


Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Diseases - 10th edition - page 329, 716-722

questions.stem: Which of the following should not be given before splenectomy?
questions.solutionHtml:
Typhoid vaccine

Typhoid vaccine should not be given to patient before splenectomy surgery

Pneumococcal, meningococcal, and Haemophilus influenzae (Hib) vaccinations are indicated for patients after splenectomy

questions.stem: In a patient with carcinoma prostate with a high Gleason score, bone scan was done. Bone scan shows increased uptake in bones but reduced uptake in kidney and soft tissue. This is reported as a super scan. Cause?

options.label: B
options.text: Due to low intake of agent by kidney and soft tissue

questions.solutionHtml:
Increased bone uptake
  • Superscan is defined as a bone scan which demonstrates markedly increased skeletal radioisotope uptake relative to soft tissues in association with absent or faint renal activity absent kidney sign
  • It occurs due to increased uptake by the bones due to presence of osteoblastic lesions of prostate metastasis.


Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease - 10th edition - page 979

questions.topic: eGurukul · Pathology - INI CET NOV 2022 (PART B)
questions.stem: Which among the following viruses is associated with Nasopharyngeal carcinoma?
questions.solutionHtml:
EBV

The Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) is linked to various types of human cancer, such as lymphoid and epithelial cancers. The most significant correlation between EBV infection and cancer is observed in undifferentiated nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), where EBV infection is believed to originate from the expansion of a single EBV-infected cell.

  • In epithelial cells, EBV infection typically leads to lytic replication.
  • However, latent infection is the primary mode of EBV infection in NPC.


Robbins basic pathology, 10th edition, Page No. 233

questions.stem: An elderly diabetic male patient underwent kidney transplantation from his twin brother. The type of grafting is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Isograft

Types of graft donors

  • Autograft - from Self
  • Allograft - from Different person of same species
  • Isograft - from Identical Twin.
  • Xenograft - from different species


Robbins basic pathology, 10th edition, Page No. 165
